facts: This is an appeal by special leave from a judgment of the Punjab High Court.
The appellant Ram Prakash Arora at the material time was the Line Superintendent, Punjab State Electricity Board, Ludhiana.
He was tried by the Special Judge on charges u/s. 5(2), read with S. 5(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and Ss. 161 and 165 of the Indian Penal Code.

He was convicted on all the counts and was sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for one year and a fine of Rs. 100/- on the first charge and to rigorous imprisonment for one year on the second charge; both the sentences were to run concurrently.
He went up in appeal to the High Court but the same was dismissed.
issues: Whether the case of the prosecution stands falsified by certain facts?
Whether the appellant had any motive to demand illegal gratification from Joginder Singh?
petitioner_arguments: The case of the prosecution stands falsified by certain facts.

If the appellant wanted any illegal gratification for facilitating the giving of the connection he would have done that on or before February 12, 1968, and before the order of sanction was made on February 13, 1968, by the S.D.O.

The explanation of the appellant was that he had gone near the shop of Joginder Singh because he was to do some work with which he was entrusted by the S.D.O. in the neighbourhood of Joginder Singh's shop.
respondent_arguments: Joginder Singh had not been informed about the sanction having been given by the S.D.O. and he must have thought that the fixing of the connection would be delayed until the demand made by the appellant was satisfied.
The evidence of Joginder Singh and Dalbir Singh has been naturally relied upon by the counsel for the State.
court_reasoning: It is highly unfair that any such inference should have been drawn when the S.D.O. was not properly cross-examined on this point.

There was no suggestion that D.S.P. Mit Singh wanted to take into possession the file relating to the connection applied for by Joginder Singh and any obstruction was placed in his way by the S.D.O. or any one else in the office of the Electricity Department.
The court should have looked askance at the conduct of investigation by the D.S.P. who had no business to wait till March 8 to take that file into possession.
holding: The appeal is allowed and the conviction is set aside.
